extracted.intended_audience: NIH/NIAID grant applicants, grant reviewers, assay developers preparing/reading grant application materials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements embedded in an NIH grant application and accompanying biosketch/budget forms, focused on developing and validating diagnostic (PANDAA/ExPAND) assays for HIV and related virology assay products. Includes technical performance targets, validation and production expectations, and form-level instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, eRA Commons user name (credential), position title, education/training table (institution, degree, completion date, field), personal statement, contributions to science, positions and honors, and complete list of published work link. Follow the prescribed layout and length limit exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay minor-variant detection sensitivity and specificity (ExPAND primary objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: The test must detect resistant variants that comprise 1% or more of the virus population or quasispecies. Sensitivity for qualitative detection of the minor variant at 1% or more must be at least 95% and specificity at least 98%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method must also yield quantitative results, showing the percentage of each resistant variant in the overall quasispecies. Intended sample population: blood specimens from HIV-infected individuals with HIV RNA viral loads above 1000 copies/ml.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative reporting of variant frequencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Assay methods must yield quantitative results, showing the percentage of each resistant variant in the overall quasispecies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond qualitative detection, assays should provide accurate quantification of the proportion of each detected resistant variant to inform clinical interpretation and downstream decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtype and drug-class coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Assays must detect mutations causing resistance to NNRTIs, NRTIs, PIs and INIs in all subtypes of HIV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and validation should ensure broad lineage/ subtype coverage so performance is retained across global HIV diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of intended clinical use by specimen viral load
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary technical objective targeted blood specimens from individuals with HIV RNA viral loads above 1000 copies/ml.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation should demonstrate assay performance at the claimed specimen viral load range; elsewhere Phase I data indicate capability to detect variants at very low frequency (<1%) from samples with low copy number (<1000 copies/mL), but the stated clinical target for the contract is >1000 copies/ml.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical limit-of-detection goals from Phase I/II validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I validation showed assays detect drug resistance variants at very low frequency (<1%) from samples with low copy number (<1000 copies/mL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase II activities include further streamlining to reduce costs and end-user labor, large scale clinical sensitivity and specificity testing, and site-to-site variability studies to confirm low-copy performance in real-world settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PANDAA PIDR+ validation and target fractional abundance
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimentally validate PANDAA reagents to quantify mutations associated with protease inhibitor resistance comprising 10% of the viral quasispecies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation plan should include experimental confirmation at the 10% fractional abundance level, plus establishment of a collaborative proficiency panel of drug-resistant and drug-sensitive HIV-1 isolates for validation benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proficiency panel requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an extensive, collaborative proficiency panel of drug resistant and drug sensitive HIV-1 isolates for assay validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the panel to validate assay accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility across relevant variant types and isolate backgrounds prior to clinical deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing and production standards (GMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce PANDAA PIDR+ under GMP conditions as part of validation and product development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assay reagents intended for clinical use must be manufactured under Good Manufacturing Practice to enable productization and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-site end-user reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that end-user, multi-site implementation of the assay is highly reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform multi-site reproducibility studies to demonstrate low site-to-site variability and confirm that intended end-users can implement the assay reliably in target settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance criteria compliance for in vitro genotyping and quantitative assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that assay performance metrics fulfill established criteria for both in vitro HIV drug resistance genotyping and quantitative assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare assay metrics against established external performance standards for HIV genotyping and quantitative molecular diagnostics (sensitivity, specificity, precision, accuracy, LOD, dynamic range).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample matrix and extraction compatibility (PANDAA HIV6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that an optimized thermostable PANDAA prototype can sensitively and specifically quantify drug resistance from HIV-1 infected whole blood, plasma, and dried blood spots using existing RNA extraction methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation should include each sample matrix intended for clinical use and demonstrate equivalent performance across matrices using practical extraction workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical market coverage by mutation panel (PANDAA HIV6)
rubrics_metrics.description: PANDAA HIV6 is intended to identify six clinically actionable HIV mutations found in >95% of patients failing a WHO-recommended first-line regimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the target mutation panel to cover the clinically most informative loci so the kit provides actionable results for the vast majority of first-line failures in target regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost, simplicity, and field-deployable design
rubrics_metrics.description: Assays must be simple, low-cost, highly sensitive, thermostable, and amenable to sample-in/answer-out workflows; they must be inexpensive since large numbers of patients would need to be screened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and development should prioritize low per-test cost, minimal hands-on time, reduced end-user labor, and robustness for resource-limited settings to enable wide-scale surveillance and point-of-care translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical validation and large-scale testing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II goals include large scale clinical sensitivity and specificity testing and site-to-site variability studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and execute clinical studies with sufficient sample size and diversity to estimate sensitivity/specificity with adequate precision and to measure inter-site variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget form equipment reporting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: List items and dollar amount for each item exceeding $5,000 in the equipment section of the Research & Related Budget form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide line-item equipment descriptions and dollar amounts for each item > $5,000; include totals for equipment requested and attach additional equipment files if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget personnel and salary reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For Senior/Key Persons and other personnel, report calendar months, academic months, summer months, requested salary, fringe benefits, and funds requested; include counts for postdoctoral associates, graduate students, undergraduate students, clerical, research associate, and total other personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Research & Related Budget sections A & B with specific months and dollar amounts for each listed role and provide total salary, wages and fringe benefits; ensure totals match supporting attachments and tracking numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget period and project dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide start date, end date, and budget period for the project (e.g., Start Date: 04-01-2019, End Date: 03-31-2020, Budget Period: 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dates are consistent across budget and project narrative and conform to the funding opportunity's allowed project periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant/trainee support reporting categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Report participant/trainee support costs by category including tuition/fees/health insurance, stipends, travel, subsistence, other, and number of participants/trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete section E to list totals per category and ensure appropriate classification of costs as participant support vs other direct costs.
